def banner(title: str) -> None:
    print()
    print("=" * 74)
    print(title)
    print("=" * 74)


def demo_1_counter_and_gap() -> None:
    banner("1.  The parity-weighted exponent counter, and the gap that never closes")
    for p, S, T in [
        (5, [1, 2], [0, 1]),
        (5, [0, 1, 2], [0, 1, 3]),
        (7, [1, 2, 4], [0, 1, 3]),
        (7, [0, 1, 2, 3], [0, 1, 2, 4]),
        (11, [0, 1, 3, 7], [2, 5, 6, 9]),
    ]:
        n = len(S)
        c = parity_counter(S, T, p)
        nz = {r: v for r, v in enumerate(c) if v != 0}
        print(f"\n p = {p:2d}   n = {n}   S = {S}   T = {T}")
        print(f"   counter c(r) = {c}")
        print(f"   nonzero at   = {nz}")
        print(f"   sum_r c(r)                     = {sum(c)}   (must be 0)")
        print(f"   max_r |c(r)|                   = {max(abs(v) for v in c)}   (must be >= 1)")
        print(f"   #supp c                        = {len(nz)}   (must be >= 2)")
        print(f"   sum_r c(r)^2                   = {sum(v * v for v in c)}   (must be >= 2)")
        assert sum(c) == 0
        assert max(abs(v) for v in c) >= 1
        assert len(nz) >= 2
        assert any(v > 0 for v in c) and any(v < 0 for v in c)
    print("\n  -> in every case the gap is open, and two-sided.")


def demo_2_determinant_identity() -> None:
    banner("2.  The counter is the determinant of a DFT minor, in disguise")
    for p, S, T in [(7, [1, 2, 4], [0, 1, 3]), (11, [0, 1, 3, 7], [2, 5, 6, 9])]:
        c = parity_counter(S, T, p)
        lhs = dft_minor_determinant(S, T, p)
        rhs = counter_to_complex(c, p)
        print(f"\n p = {p}   S = {S}   T = {T}")
        print(f"   det( omega^(S_j T_k) )   = {lhs:.10f}")
        print(f"   sum_r c(r) omega^r       = {rhs:.10f}")
        print(f"   |difference|             = {abs(lhs - rhs):.3e}")
        print(f"   |det|                    = {abs(lhs):.10f}   (nonzero: Chebotarev)")
        assert abs(lhs - rhs) < 1e-9
        assert abs(lhs) > 1e-9


def demo_3_exhaustive_chebotarev() -> None:
    banner("3.  Exhaustive check of Chebotarev's theorem for small primes")
    for p in (5, 7):
        for n in range(2, min(p, 4) + 1):
            worst = None
            count = 0
            for S in itertools.permutations(range(p), n):
                for T in itertools.permutations(range(p), n):
                    c = parity_counter(S, T, p)
                    peak = max(abs(v) for v in c)
                    count += 1
                    if worst is None or peak < worst[0]:
                        worst = (peak, S, T)
            assert worst is not None and worst[0] >= 1
            print(
                f"  p = {p}, n = {n}:  {count:7d} injective pairs tested, "
                f"min over pairs of max_r|c(r)| = {worst[0]}  "
                f"(attained e.g. at S={list(worst[1])}, T={list(worst[2])})"
            )
    print("\n  -> the parity gap never closes: the minimum of max_r|c(r)| is always >= 1.")


def demo_4_minimal_length_witness() -> None:
    banner("4.  The minimal-Coxeter-length witness")
    for p, S, T in [(7, [1, 2, 4], [0, 1, 3]), (11, [0, 1, 3, 7], [2, 5, 6, 9])]:
        r, val, sigma = minimal_length_witness(S, T, p)
        fibre = [
            perm
            for perm in itertools.permutations(range(len(S)))
            if perm_exponent(S, T, perm, p) == r
        ]
        print(f"\n p = {p}   S = {S}   T = {T}")
        print(f"   extremal residue r* = {r},  c(r*) = {val},  |c(r*)| >= 1  OK")
        print(f"   fibre over r* has {len(fibre)} permutations")
        print(f"   minimal-length witness sigma = {sigma}, length l(sigma) = {coxeter_length(sigma)}")
        print(f"   lengths in the fibre = {sorted(coxeter_length(t) for t in fibre)}")
        print(f"   sign(sigma) = {permutation_sign(sigma)} = (-1)^l = {(-1) ** coxeter_length(sigma)}")
        assert permutation_sign(sigma) == (-1) ** coxeter_length(sigma)
        assert coxeter_length(sigma) == min(coxeter_length(t) for t in fibre)


def demo_5_composite_closure() -> None:
    banner("5.  Over composite moduli the gap CLOSES — and primality is detected")
    print("\n  (a) the smallest closure: m = 4, S = T = (0, 2)")
    c = parity_counter([0, 2], [0, 2], 4)
    print(f"      counter = {c}   -> identically zero, the gap has closed")
    assert all(v == 0 for v in c)

    print("\n  (b) annihilating progressions S(i) = a i, T(j) = b j over m = a b")
    for a, b, n in [(2, 3, 2), (3, 3, 3), (2, 5, 2), (4, 3, 3)]:
        S, T, m = annihilating_progressions(a, b, n)
        c = parity_counter(S, T, m)
        ok = all(v == 0 for v in c)
        print(f"      m = {m:2d} = {a}*{b},  n = {n},  S = {S}, T = {T}  ->  closed: {ok}")
        assert ok

    print("\n  (c) primality test by exhaustive search at width n = 2")
    for m in range(2, 16):
        closed = False
        for S in itertools.permutations(range(m), 2):
            for T in itertools.permutations(range(m), 2):
                if all(v == 0 for v in parity_counter(S, T, m)):
                    closed = True
                    break
            if closed:
                break
        is_prime = m > 1 and all(m % d for d in range(2, int(m ** 0.5) + 1))
        verdict = "COMPOSITE" if closed else "PRIME    "
        print(f"      m = {m:2d}:  gap closes at n=2? {str(closed):5s}  -> {verdict}"
              f"   (truth: {'prime' if is_prime else 'composite'})")
        assert closed == (not is_prime)
    print("\n  -> gap closes  <=>  modulus is composite.")


def demo_6_width_of_closure() -> None:
    banner("6.  How wide a closed gap can be (even moduli: exactly m - 2)")
    for m in (4, 6):
        q = least_prime_factor(m)
        print(f"\n  modulus m = {m} (least prime factor q = {q}); predicted max width = m - q = {m - q}")
        for n in range(2, m + 1):
            closed = False
            witness = None
            for S in itertools.permutations(range(m), n):
                for T in itertools.permutations(range(m), n):
                    if all(v == 0 for v in parity_counter(S, T, m)):
                        closed, witness = True, (S, T)
                        break
                if closed:
                    break
            tag = "CLOSES" if closed else "open  "
            extra = f"  e.g. S={list(witness[0])}, T={list(witness[1])}" if witness else ""
            print(f"      n = {n}:  {tag}   (theory: {'closes' if n <= m - q else 'open'}){extra}")
            assert closed == (n <= m - q)
    print("\n  -> matches the theorem exactly: closure at every width 2..m-2, never at m-1 or m.")


def demo_7_uncertainty() -> None:
    banner("7.  The additive uncertainty principle  |supp f| + |supp f_hat| >= p + 1")
    for p in (5, 7):
        print(f"\n  p = {p}: scanning all 0/1-valued nonzero f on Z/{p}")
        worst = None
        for mask in range(1, 1 << p):
            f = [1.0 if (mask >> x) & 1 else 0.0 for x in range(p)]
            a, b = support_size(f), support_size(dft(f, p))
            if worst is None or a + b < worst[0]:
                worst = (a + b, mask, a, b)
            assert a + b >= p + 1, (mask, a, b)
        assert worst is not None
        supp = [x for x in range(p) if (worst[1] >> x) & 1]
        print(f"      minimum of |supp f| + |supp f_hat| = {worst[0]}   (bound: {p + 1})")
        print(f"      attained by f = indicator of {supp}  ({worst[2]} + {worst[3]})")
    print("\n  Contrast with a composite modulus, where the additive bound FAILS:")
    for m, sub in [(4, [0, 2]), (6, [0, 2, 4]), (9, [0, 3, 6])]:
        f = [1.0 if x in sub else 0.0 for x in range(m)]
        a, b = support_size(f), support_size(dft(f, m))
        print(f"      m = {m}: f = indicator of the subgroup {sub}: "
              f"|supp f| + |supp f_hat| = {a} + {b} = {a + b}  <  m + 1 = {m + 1}")
        assert a + b < m + 1
        print(f"                 but the multiplicative bound survives: {a} * {b} = {a * b} >= {m}")


def demo_8_pi_adic_depth() -> None:
    banner("8.  pi-adic depth of the integral minor:  pi^{n(n-1)/2} | det")
    for p, cases in [
        (5, [([1, 2], [0, 1]), ([0, 1, 2], [0, 1, 3])]),
        (7, [([1, 3], [2, 5]), ([1, 2, 4], [0, 1, 3])]),
    ]:
        for S, T in cases:
            n = len(S)
            elt = integral_minor_in_cyclotomic(S, T, p)
            depth = pi_adic_depth(elt, p)
            predicted = n * (n - 1) // 2
            print(f"  p = {p}, n = {n}, S = {S}, T = {T}:  "
                  f"v_pi(det) = {depth}   (lower bound n(n-1)/2 = {predicted})")
            assert depth >= predicted


def demo_9_rigidity() -> None:
    banner("9.  Mod-p rigidity:  n(n-1)/2 >= p - 1  =>  all c(r) congruent mod p")
    for p, S, T in [
        (3, [0, 1, 2], [0, 1, 2]),
        (5, [0, 1, 2, 3], [0, 1, 2, 3]),
        (5, [0, 1, 2, 3, 4], [0, 2, 4, 1, 3]),
        (7, [0, 1, 2, 3], [0, 1, 2, 3]),
        (7, [0, 1, 2, 3], [0, 1, 2, 4]),
        (7, [0, 1, 2, 3], [0, 1, 2, 6]),
    ]:
        n = len(S)
        depth = n * (n - 1) // 2
        c = parity_counter(S, T, p)
        residues = sorted({v % p for v in c})
        rigid_regime = depth >= p - 1
        print(f"\n  p = {p}, n = {n}:  n(n-1)/2 = {depth}, p - 1 = {p - 1}  "
              f"-> rigid regime: {rigid_regime}")
        print(f"      counter          = {c}")
        print(f"      residues mod {p}   = {residues}")
        if rigid_regime:
            assert len(residues) == 1, "rigidity must force a single residue class"
            lam = residues[0]
            if lam != 0:
                print(f"      common residue {lam} != 0  ->  FULL SUPPORT (no c(r) is zero)")
                assert all(v != 0 for v in c)
            else:
                peak = max(abs(v) for v in c)
                print(f"      common residue 0  ->  peak |c(r)| = {peak} >= p = {p}")
                assert peak >= p

"""

The additive uncertainty principle for a prime modulus,

    |supp f| + |supp f_hat| >= p + 1   for every nonzero f : Z/p -> C,

has an immediate and very concrete consequence: a k-sparse signal on Z/p is uniquely
determined by ANY 2k of its Fourier coefficients, provided 2k <= p.  If two k-sparse
signals agreed on a set Xi of 2k frequencies, their difference g would be 2k-sparse with
g_hat vanishing on Xi, so |supp g| + |supp g_hat| <= 2k + (p - 2k) = p, which is forbidden.

Uniqueness is not merely abstract: because every square minor of the Fourier matrix of Z/p
is nonsingular, the recovery is a plain linear solve once the support is known, and the
support can be found by brute force over the (p choose k) candidates for small k.  This
script demonstrates both the uniqueness and the reconstruction, and then shows that the
guarantee collapses over a composite modulus.

Requires only the Python standard library.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import cmath
import itertools
import random
from typing import Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple

Complex = complex


def dft(f: Sequence[Complex], m: int) -> List[Complex]:
    w = cmath.exp(-2j * cmath.pi / m)
    return [sum(f[x] * w ** (x * xi) for x in range(m)) for xi in range(m)]


def support(v: Sequence[Complex], tol: float = 1e-8) -> List[int]:
    return [i for i, z in enumerate(v) if abs(z) > tol]


def solve_linear(A: List[List[Complex]], b: List[Complex]) -> List[Complex]:
    """Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting on a square complex system."""
    n = len(A)
    M = [row[:] + [b[i]] for i, row in enumerate(A)]
    for col in range(n):
        piv = max(range(col, n), key=lambda r: abs(M[r][col]))
        if abs(M[piv][col]) < 1e-12:
            raise ValueError("singular system — impossible for a prime-modulus DFT minor")
        M[col], M[piv] = M[piv], M[col]
        inv = 1.0 / M[col][col]
        M[col] = [z * inv for z in M[col]]
        for r in range(n):
            if r != col and abs(M[r][col]) > 0:
                factor = M[r][col]
                M[r] = [M[r][c] - factor * M[col][c] for c in range(n + 1)]
    return [M[i][n] for i in range(n)]


def recover_sparse(
    samples: Dict[int, Complex], m: int, k: int
) -> Tuple[List[int], List[Complex]]:
    """Find the unique k-sparse signal matching the given Fourier samples.

    Tries every candidate support of size k; for each one, solves the linear system given
    by the sampled frequencies (using k of them) and checks the remaining samples.
    """
    freqs = sorted(samples)
    w = cmath.exp(-2j * cmath.pi / m)
    for cand in itertools.combinations(range(m), k):
        A = [[w ** (x * xi) for x in cand] for xi in freqs[:k]]
        try:
            sol = solve_linear(A, [samples[xi] for xi in freqs[:k]])
        except ValueError:
            continue
        ok = True
        for xi in freqs[k:]:
            val = sum(sol[i] * w ** (cand[i] * xi) for i in range(k))
            if abs(val - samples[xi]) > 1e-7:
                ok = False
                break
        if ok:
            return list(cand), sol
    raise RuntimeError("no k-sparse signal matches the samples")


def demo_recovery(p: int, k: int, seed: int = 7) -> None:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    print(f"\n  p = {p}, sparsity k = {k}, using 2k = {2*k} Fourier samples")
    truth_support = sorted(rng.sample(range(p), k))
    values = [complex(rng.randint(-4, 4) or 3, rng.randint(-4, 4)) for _ in range(k)]
    f = [0j] * p
    for x, v in zip(truth_support, values):
        f[x] = v
    fh = dft(f, p)
    freqs = sorted(rng.sample(range(p), 2 * k))
    samples = {xi: fh[xi] for xi in freqs}
    print(f"    true support   = {truth_support}")
    print(f"    sampled freqs  = {freqs}")
    supp, sol = recover_sparse(samples, p, k)
    err = max(abs(sol[i] - f[supp[i]]) for i in range(k))
    print(f"    recovered supp = {supp}   (match: {supp == truth_support})")
    print(f"    max coefficient error = {err:.2e}")
    print(f"    uncertainty check: |supp f| + |supp f_hat| = "
          f"{len(support(f))} + {len(support(fh))} = "
          f"{len(support(f)) + len(support(fh))}  >=  p + 1 = {p + 1}")
    assert supp == truth_support and err < 1e-7


def demo_composite_failure(m: int) -> None:
    """Over Z/m with m composite, 2k Fourier samples can fail to determine a k-sparse signal."""
    print(f"\n  m = {m}")
    best = None
    for d in range(2, m):
        if m % d:
            continue
        sub = list(range(0, m, d))                  # subgroup of order m/d
        f = [1.0 + 0j if x in sub else 0j for x in range(m)]
        fh = dft(f, m)
        a, b = len(support(f)), len(support(fh))
        missing = m - b
        print(f"    indicator of the subgroup of order {a} = {sub}:")
        print(f"        |supp f| = {a}, |supp f_hat| = {b}, sum = {a + b} < m + 1 = {m + 1}"
              f"   (additive bound violated)")
        print(f"        product {a} * {b} = {a * b} >= {m}   (multiplicative bound intact)")
        if missing >= 2 * a and (best is None or missing - 2 * a > best[0]):

def permutation_sign(perm: Sequence[int]) -> int:

    """Number of inversions: pairs i < j with perm[i] > perm[j]."""

    return c

    c = parity_counter(S, T, m)
    r_star = max(range(m), key=lambda r: abs(c[r]))
    return r_star, c[r_star]


def bruhat_bfs_witness(
    S: Sequence[int], T: Sequence[int], m: int, target: int

    Bset = {x % m for x in B}

    classes = len(set(kappa))
    if classes >= len(J):
        return False, f"(3) fails: {classes} classes but |J| = {len(J)}"
    return True, (f"valid: |J| = {len(J)} rows, subgroup B of order {len(Bset)}, "
                  f"{classes} column classes < |J|")


def build_closure_certificate(m: int, n: int) -> Optional[Dict[str, object]]:
    """Canonical closure data for a composite modulus at width n, when 2 <= n <= m - q."""
    q = least_prime_factor(m)
    if q == m:
        return None                                   # prime: closure is impossible
    a = m // q
    if not (2 <= n <= m - q):
        return None                                   # outside the proved window
    c = -(-n // q)                                    # ceil(n / q) column classes
    assert c + 1 <= a, "the window n <= m - q guarantees room for |J| = c + 1 rows"

    # rows: the first c + 1 of them carry the multiples of q, which pairwise annihilate B
    J_values = [q * t % m for t in range(c + 1)]
    spare = [x for x in range(m) if x not in set(J_values)]
    S = J_values + spare[: n - (c + 1)]
    J = set(range(c + 1))

    # columns: pack n residues into c classes modulo m/q, each class of size q
    step = m // q                                     # = a; classes are t + <a>
    T: List[int] = []
    kappa: List[int] = []
    for cls in range(c):
        for t in range(q):
            if len(T) == n:
                break
            T.append((cls + t * step) % m)
            kappa.append(cls)
    B = subgroup_generated(step, m)                   # subgroup of order q
    return {"m": m, "n": n, "q": q, "S": S, "T": T, "J": J, "B": B, "kappa": kappa}


def certified_closure(m: int, n: int) -> Dict[str, object]:
    data = build_closure_certificate(m, n)
    if data is None:
        return {"m": m, "n": n, "closure_certified": False,
                "reason": "prime modulus, or width outside the proved window [2, m - q]"}
    ok, msg = verify_pigeonhole_certificate(
        data["S"], data["T"], m, data["J"], data["B"], data["kappa"])
    return {**data, "closure_certified": ok, "message": msg}

    n = len(S)
    counter = [0] * m

        seen = [False] * n
        sign = 1
        for start in range(n):

            while not seen[x]:
                seen[x] = True
                x = perm[x]
                length += 1
            if length % 2 == 0:
                sign = -sign
        counter[e] += sign
    return all(v == 0 for v in counter)

def minor_in_cyclotomic(S: Sequence[int], T: Sequence[int], p: int) -> List[int]:
    """det(zeta^{S_j T_k}) in the Z-basis 1, zeta, ..., zeta^{p-2}."""
    counter = parity_counter(S, T, p)
    top = counter[p - 1]
    return [counter[k] - top for k in range(p - 1)]


def divide_by_pi(coeffs: List[int], p: int) -> Optional[List[int]]:
    """Exact division by pi = zeta - 1, or None if not divisible."""
    total = sum(coeffs)
    if total % p != 0:
        return None
    c = -total // p
    B = [coeffs[k] + c for k in range(p - 1)] + [c]
    Q = [0] * (p - 1)
    Q[p - 2] = B[p - 1]
    for k in range(p - 2, 0, -1):
        Q[k - 1] = B[k] + Q[k]
    assert B[0] + Q[0] == 0
    return Q

    cur, depth = list(coeffs), 0
    while depth < cap:
        nxt = divide_by_pi(cur, p)
        if nxt is None:
            return depth
        cur, depth = nxt, depth + 1
    return depth

  <details>
    <summary>What is Coxeter length, and why does it appear?</summary>
    <p>The <b>Coxeter length</b> ℓ(σ) of a permutation is its number of inversions:
    pairs i < j with σ(i) > σ(j). Equivalently it is the least number of
    <em>adjacent</em> swaps needed to build σ. Length and sign are linked by
    sgn(σ) = (−1)<sup>ℓ(σ)</sup>, and ℓ(σ) = 0 only for the
    identity. The sharpened form of the theorem asks for a canonical certificate: among all
    permutations realising the extremal residue, take the one closest to the identity.</p>
  </details>
</div>

<details class="panel">
  <summary><b>Why does a prime modulus force the gap open?</b> (click for the argument)</summary>
  <p>Let ζ be a primitive p-th root of unity. Expanding by the Leibniz formula, the
  determinant of the matrix M<sub>jk</sub> = ζ<sup>S(j)T(k)</sup> — a minor of the
  Fourier matrix of Z/p — equals ∑<sub>r</sub> c(r)ζ<sup>r</sup>. So the gap stays
  open exactly when that minor is nonsingular.</p>
  <p>Suppose it were singular. Then there is a nonzero kernel vector w over Z[ζ], which we
  normalise so that not all coordinates are divisible by the ramified prime
  π = ζ − 1. The polynomial f(X) = ∑<sub>k</sub> w<sub>k</sub>X<sup>T(k)</sup>
  then vanishes at the n <em>distinct</em> points ζ<sup>S(j)</sup>, so it is divisible by
  ∏<sub>j</sub>(X − ζ<sup>S(j)</sup>).</p>
  <p>Now reduce modulo π. This collapses every power of ζ to 1, so all n distinct roots
  fuse into a single root of multiplicity n: over F<sub>p</sub> we get
  (X−1)<sup>n</sup> dividing a nonzero polynomial of degree < p with at most n terms.
  But a nonzero polynomial over F<sub>p</sub> of degree less than p that is divisible by
  (X−1)<sup>n</sup> must have <em>more</em> than n terms — differentiate repeatedly and
  count. Contradiction.</p>
  <p>Both hypotheses are used: primality makes ζ of order exactly p (distinct roots) and
  keeps the degree below p (so differentiation destroys only the constant term). Over a composite
  modulus the statement is simply false, as the presets above demonstrate.</p>
</details>

<script>
function permutations(n) {
  const out = [], a = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) a.push(i);
  (function rec(k) {
    if (k === n) { out.push(a.slice()); return; }
    for (let i = k; i < n; i++) {
      const t = a[k]; a[k] = a[i]; a[i] = t;
      rec(k+1);
      const u = a[k]; a[k] = a[i]; a[i] = u;
    }
  })(0);
  return out;
}
function sign(p) {
  const n = p.length, seen = new Array(n).fill(false);
  let s = 1;
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (seen[i]) continue;
    let len = 0, j = i;
    while (!seen[j]) { seen[j] = true; j = p[j]; len++; }
    if (len % 2 === 0) s = -s;
  }
  return s;
}
function inversions(p) {
  let c = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < p.length; i++)
    for (let j = i+1; j < p.length; j++) if (p[i] > p[j]) c++;
  return c;
}
function parse(str) {
  return str.split(",").map(function (s) { return s.trim(); })
            .filter(function (s) { return s.length; }).map(Number);
}
function isPrimeNum(m) {
  if (m < 2) return false;
  for (let d = 2; d * d <= m; d++) if (m % d === 0) return false;
  return true;
}

function compute() {
  const errEl = document.getElementById("err");
  errEl.textContent = "";

  const S = parse(document.getElementById("S").value);
  const T = parse(document.getElementById("T").value);
  if (!(m >= 2)) { errEl.textContent = "Modulus must be at least 2."; return; }
  if (S.length !== T.length) { errEl.textContent = "S and T must have the same length."; return; }
  const n = S.length;
  if (n < 1 || n > 7) { errEl.textContent = "Use a width between 1 and 7."; return; }
  for (const v of S.concat(T))

      errEl.textContent = "All entries must be integers in 0 .. " + (m-1) + "."; return; }

    e = ((e % m) + m) % m;
    c[e] += sign(p);
    if (!fibres.has(e)) fibres.set(e, []);
    fibres.get(e).push(p);
  }

  const supp = c.filter(function (v) { return v !== 0; }).length;
  const total = c.reduce(function (a,b) { return a+b; }, 0);
  const prime = isPrimeNum(m);

  const verdict = document.getElementById("verdict");
  if (peak === 0) {
    verdict.className = "verdict closed";
    verdict.textContent = "GAP CLOSED  \u2014  c(r) = 0 for every residue r." +

  } else {
    verdict.className = "verdict open";
    verdict.textContent = "GAP OPEN  \u2014  max |c(r)| = " + peak +
      (prime ? "   (forced, since m = " + m + " is prime)" :
               "   (this particular pair happens not to cancel)");
  }

  document.getElementById("stats").innerHTML =
    '<span class="stat">n! = <b>' + perms.length + '</b></span>' +
    '<span class="stat">∑ c(r) = <b>' + total + '</b></span>' +
    '<span class="stat">|supp c| = <b>' + supp + '</b> / ' + m + '</span>' +
    '<span class="stat">∑ c(r)² = <b>' +
      c.reduce(function (a,b) { return a+b*b; }, 0) + '</b></span>' +
    '<span class="stat">n(n−1)/2 = <b>' + (n*(n-1)/2) +
      '</b> vs m−1 = <b>' + (m-1) + '</b></span>';

  const scale = peak === 0 ? 1 : peak;
  const chart = document.getElementById("chart");
  const axis = document.getElementById("axis");
  chart.innerHTML = ""; axis.innerHTML = "";
  for (let r = 0; r < m; r++) {
    const col = document.createElement("div");
    col.className = "bar-col";
    const h = Math.round(85 * Math.abs(c[r]) / scale);
    const bar = document.createElement("div");
    bar.className = "bar " + (c[r] >= 0 ? "p" : "n");
    bar.style.height = h + "%";

      const lab = document.createElement("div");
      lab.className = "val";
      lab.style.bottom = (h + 2) + "%";
      lab.textContent = c[r];
      col.appendChild(lab);
    }
    col.appendChild(bar);
    chart.appendChild(col);
    const sp = document.createElement("span");
    sp.textContent = r;
    axis.appendChild(sp);
  }

  const wEl = document.getElementById("witness");
  if (peak === 0) {
    wEl.innerHTML = "<p>The counter vanishes identically, so there is no extremal residue: " +
      "every fibre cancels perfectly. This is exactly what the theorem forbids over a prime " +
      "modulus.</p>";
  } else {
    let rStar = 0;
    for (let r = 1; r < m; r++) if (Math.abs(c[r]) > Math.abs(c[rStar])) rStar = r;
    const fib = fibres.get(rStar) || [];
    let best = null, bl = Infinity;
    for (const p of fib) { const l = inversions(p); if (l < bl) { bl = l; best = p; } }
    wEl.innerHTML =
      '<p>Extremal residue <code>r* = ' + rStar + '</code> with <code>c(r*) = ' + c[rStar] +
      '</code>, so <code>|c(r*)| = ' + Math.abs(c[rStar]) + ' ≥ 1</code>. Its fibre contains ' +
      fib.length + ' permutations.</p>' +
      '<p>Minimal-Coxeter-length witness: <code>σ = [' + best.join(", ") + ']</code> with ' +
      '<code>ℓ(σ) = ' + bl + '</code> inversions and ' +
      '<code>sgn(σ) = ' + sign(best) + ' = (−1)^' + bl + '</code>.</p>' +
      '<p>Lengths occurring in that fibre: <code>[' +
      fib.map(inversions).sort(function (a,b) { return a-b; }).join(", ") + ']</code>.</p>';
  }

  const rows = [];
  for (let r = 0; r < m; r++) {
    const f = fibres.get(r) || [];
    const ev = f.filter(function (p) { return sign(p) === 1; }).length;
    rows.push("<tr><td>" + r + "</td><td>" + f.length + "</td><td>" + ev + "</td><td>" +
      (f.length - ev) + "</td><td style='color:" +
      (c[r] > 0 ? "var(--pos)" : c[r] < 0 ? "var(--neg)" : "var(--muted)") + "'>" +
      c[r] + "</td></tr>");
  }
  document.getElementById("fibres").innerHTML =
    "<table><tr><th>residue r</th><th>fibre size</th><th>even</th><th>odd</th>" +
    "<th>c(r) = even − odd</th></tr>" + rows.join("") + "</table>";
}

document.getElementById("go").addEventListener("click", compute);
document.getElementById("preset").addEventListener("change", function () {
  const parts = this.value.split("|");
  document.getElementById("m").value = parts[0];
  document.getElementById("S").value = parts[1];
  document.getElementById("T").value = parts[2];
  compute();
});
document.getElementById("rand").addEventListener("click", function () {
  const m = parseInt(document.getElementById("m").value, 10);
  const n = Math.min(parse(document.getElementById("S").value).length || 3, m);
  function pick() {
    const pool = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < m; i++) pool.push(i);
    for (let i = pool.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
      const j = Math.floor(Math.random() * (i+1));
      const t = pool[i]; pool[i] = pool[j]; pool[j] = t;
    }
    return pool.slice(0, n);
  }
  document.getElementById("S").value = pick().join(",");
  document.getElementById("T").value = pick().join(",");
  compute();
});
compute();
</script>

<details class="panel">
  <summary><b>Why the additive bound is a theorem about determinants</b></summary>
  <p>Suppose <code>f</code> is supported on a set A and its transform vanishes on a set C, with
  |A| = |C| = n. Restricting the Fourier matrix to rows C and columns A gives an
  n×n submatrix of the Fourier matrix of Z/m, and the statement "f lives on A and
  f̂ dies on C" says exactly that this submatrix has a nonzero kernel vector, i.e. that it
  is <b>singular</b>.</p>
  <p>For a <b>prime</b> modulus, no square submatrix of the Fourier matrix is ever singular. So
  such an f cannot exist, and one gets
  <code>|supp f| + |supp f̂| ≥ p + 1</code>: a signal with k nonzero samples has a
  spectrum missing at most k−1 frequencies.</p>
  <p>For a <b>composite</b> modulus m = ab, singular submatrices abound, and the indicator
  function of the subgroup of order a is the standard witness: it has support a and spectrum of
  support b, so the sum is a + b, which can be as small as 2√m. The weaker multiplicative
  bound <code>|supp f|·|supp f̂| ≥ m</code> survives over every cyclic group, and
  the subgroup indicators show it is sharp there.</p>
  <p>A striking consequence over primes: any k-sparse signal is uniquely determined by any 2k of
  its Fourier coefficients (provided 2k ≤ p). If two k-sparse signals agreed on 2k
  frequencies, their difference would be 2k-sparse with 2k vanishing Fourier coefficients, giving
  a support sum of at most p — impossible.</p>
</details>

### A guided tour of the parity-weighted exponent counter, Chebotarev's theorem, and the sharpest uncertainty principle on a cyclic group

---

## 1. A strange tournament

Fix a modulus $m$ and two lists of **distinct** residues modulo $m$:

$$S = (S_1, \dots, S_n), \qquad T = (T_1, \dots, T_n), \qquad S_i, T_j \in \mathbb{Z}/m .$$

A *matching* of the two lists is a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1, \dots, n\}$, and every matching gets a single number, its **exponent**:

$$E_\sigma \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{n} S_{\sigma(j)}\, T_j \pmod m .$$

There are $n!$ matchings but only $m$ possible exponents, so when $n!$ is large the exponents pile up. Now weight each matching by its **sign** — $+1$ if it is a product of an even number of swaps, $-1$ otherwise — and count the imbalance at each residue:

$$\boxed{\;c_{S,T}(r) \;=\; \sum_{\substack{\sigma \\ E_\sigma = r}} \operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\;}$$

This is the **parity-weighted exponent counter**. It is an integer-valued function on $\mathbb{Z}/m$, and it has one guaranteed property: because exactly half of all permutations are even once $n \geq 2$, its total mass vanishes,

$$\sum_{r} c_{S,T}(r) = 0 .$$

The even and odd matchings are in perfect *global* balance. **Question:** can they also be in perfect *local* balance — can $c_{S,T}(r) = 0$ for every single $r$?

---

## 2. Play with it first

Before any theory, get your hands on the object. Try a few prime moduli, then flip to the composite presets and watch what happens.

{{interactive_demo:0}}

> **What to look for.** Over a prime modulus, no matter how you choose the two lists, at least one bar is nonzero — in fact there is always at least one green bar *and* one red bar, since the bars must sum to zero. Over $m = 4$ with $S = T = (0,2)$ the entire chart is flat. That single example already tells you the answer depends on arithmetic, not combinatorics.

<details>
<summary><b>Why injectivity is not a technicality</b></summary>

If two entries of $S$ coincide, say $S_{i_1} = S_{i_2}$, then replacing $\sigma$ by $\sigma \circ (i_1\,i_2)$ leaves every exponent unchanged while flipping every sign. Every fibre then cancels for a completely trivial reason, and the counter is identically zero. Injectivity is precisely the hypothesis that makes the question interesting — which is why the widget refuses repeated entries.
</details>

---

## 3. The theorem

> **Theorem (the parity gap never closes).** Let $p$ be prime and let $S, T$ be lists of $n$ distinct residues modulo $p$. Then $c_{S,T}(r) \neq 0$ for some $r$, hence $\max_r |c_{S,T}(r)| \geq 1$. Moreover the maximum is attained at a residue of the form $E_\sigma$ for a permutation $\sigma$ of minimal **Coxeter length** — minimal number of inversions — among all permutations with that exponent.

And its exact converse:

> **Theorem (primality detection).** For a modulus $m \geq 2$, some injective pair of some width $n \geq 2$ has an identically vanishing counter **if and only if $m$ is composite.**

The parity gap is a primality test written entirely in the language of signed permutation counts.

---

## 4. The disguise: it is really a determinant

Here is the observation that turns a combinatorial question into an algebraic one. Let $\zeta$ be a primitive $p$-th root of unity, and form the $n \times n$ matrix

$$M_{jk} = \zeta^{\,S_j T_k}.$$

This is a **minor of the discrete Fourier transform matrix** of $\mathbb{Z}/p$ — the $p \times p$ matrix $(\zeta^{ab})$, carved down to the rows listed by $S$ and the columns listed by $T$. Expand its determinant by the Leibniz formula:

$$\det M = \sum_\sigma \operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_j \zeta^{S_{\sigma(j)}T_j} = \sum_\sigma \operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\,\zeta^{E_\sigma} = \sum_{r} c_{S,T}(r)\,\zeta^{r}.$$

The counter *is* the coefficient list of the determinant. So:

$$\text{parity gap stays open} \iff \det M \neq 0 \iff \text{every DFT minor of } \mathbb{Z}/p \text{ is nonsingular}.$$

That last statement is **Chebotarev's theorem on roots of unity**, a result of striking strength: the Fourier matrix of a prime cyclic group has *no* singular square submatrix, of any size, anywhere.

---

## 5. The proof in four moves

The whole argument runs through one arithmetic accident: in the ring $\mathbb{Z}[\zeta]$ generated by a primitive $p$-th root of unity, the prime $p$ is **totally ramified**. Setting $\pi = \zeta - 1$, one has $\pi \mid p$, and $p$ is a unit times $\pi^{p-1}$. There is a single reduction map

$$\mathrm{red} \colon \mathbb{Z}[\zeta] \to \mathbb{F}_p, \qquad \zeta \mapsto 1,$$

whose kernel is exactly the multiples of $\pi$. It is brutally lossy — every power of $\zeta$ collapses to $1$ — and that is exactly why it is useful.

<details>
<summary><b>Click to reveal the full argument</b></summary>

Suppose $\det M = 0$.

**Move 1 — a primitive kernel vector.** Since $\mathbb{Z}[\zeta]$ is a domain, a vanishing determinant produces a nonzero vector $v$ with $Mv = 0$. Divide out the largest power of $\pi$ dividing all coordinates: this is possible because no nonzero element of $\mathbb{Z}[\zeta]$ is divisible by arbitrarily high powers of $\pi$ (Krull's intersection theorem in a Noetherian domain). We obtain $v = \pi^m w$ with $Mw = 0$ and $\mathrm{red}(w_{k_0}) \neq 0$ for some coordinate.

**Move 2 — a sparse polynomial.** Put
$$f(X) = \sum_{k} w_k X^{T_k},$$
reading each $T_k$ as an integer in $\{0,\dots,p-1\}$. The relation $Mw=0$ says exactly that $f(\zeta^{S_j}) = 0$ for every $j$. Because $S$ is injective and $\zeta$ has order exactly $p$, the $n$ evaluation points are pairwise **distinct**, so
$$\prod_{j}\bigl(X - \zeta^{S_j}\bigr) \ \Big|\ f(X).$$
Note that nothing is wrong yet: over a field a polynomial with $n$ terms may perfectly well have $n$ roots.

**Move 3 — collapse.** Apply $\mathrm{red}$ coefficientwise. Every root $\zeta^{S_j}$ becomes $1$, so all $n$ distinct roots **fuse into a single root of multiplicity $n$**:
$$(X-1)^n \ \Big|\ \bar f(X) \quad\text{in } \mathbb{F}_p[X],$$
where $\bar f \neq 0$ (thanks to Move 1), $\deg \bar f < p$ (the exponents are residues), and $\bar f$ has at most $n$ terms.

**Move 4 — sparse polynomials cannot be that degenerate.**

> **Sparse-multiplicity lemma.** A nonzero $f \in \mathbb{F}_p[X]$ with $\deg f < p$ divisible by $(X-1)^n$ has **strictly more than $n$** nonzero coefficients.

*Proof by descent.* Factor out the largest power of $X$ — this changes neither the number of terms nor divisibility by $(X-1)^n$, since $X$ and $X-1$ are coprime — so the constant term is nonzero. Differentiate: the derivative is divisible by $(X-1)^{n-1}$, loses the constant term, and loses nothing else, because a term $cX^e$ becomes $ecX^{e-1}$ with $e \not\equiv 0 \bmod p$. Here the degree bound $\deg f < p$ is doing all the work. So the derivative has exactly one term fewer and one less multiplicity; induct.

**Contradiction.** Move 3 produced at most $n$ terms; Move 4 demands more than $n$. Hence $\det M \neq 0$. $\blacksquare$

The moral: the ramified prime converts *separation of roots* into *multiplicity at a single root*, and multiplicity is what sparse polynomials cannot afford in characteristic $p$.
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Why one cannot simply reduce modulo $p$</b></summary>

Because the determinant is genuinely divisible by $p$ once $n$ is large. Taylor-expanding each row at $\zeta^{S_j} = 1 + u_j$ and using the alternating property of the determinant, the surviving terms have pairwise distinct Taylor orders, so
$$\pi^{\binom n 2} \ \Big|\ \det M .$$
Since $p \sim \pi^{p-1}$, as soon as $\binom n2 \geq p-1$ the whole minor lies in $p\,\mathbb{Z}[\zeta]$ and reduction mod $p$ sees nothing at all. The finer prime $\pi$ resolves $p$ into $p-1$ layers and lets the argument find the one layer where information survives.
</details>

---

## 6. Seeing it at scale

{{visualization:0}}

The top row shows counters over prime moduli: never flat. The bottom row shows composite moduli where the counter is identically zero. The closure map on the right summarises everything known: green cells are widths at which the gap provably cannot close (all widths for a prime modulus; and the top two widths $n = m-1$, $n = m$ for every modulus), red cells are widths where an explicit construction closes it, and the thin amber strip marks the remaining unknown window for odd composite moduli.

---

## 7. Computing the counter — three algorithms

The definitional algorithm is honest and hopeless: $n!$ permutations.

{{algorithm:0}}

For the sharpened form of the theorem we need a **canonical witness**: a permutation realising the extremal residue with the fewest inversions. Rather than sorting all $n!$ permutations by length, we walk the symmetric group in the weak Bruhat order, which is graded by length, and stop at the first hit.

{{algorithm:2}}

<details>
<summary><b>What is Coxeter length?</b></summary>

The Coxeter length $\ell(\sigma)$ counts inversions: pairs $i<j$ with $\sigma(i)>\sigma(j)$. Equivalently, it is the least number of *adjacent* transpositions needed to write $\sigma$ — the word length in the standard presentation of the symmetric group as a [Coxeter group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coxeter_group). Length and sign are tied together by
$$\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma) = (-1)^{\ell(\sigma)},$$
and $\ell(\sigma)=0$ only for the identity. Asking for the shortest witness is asking for the matching closest to "do nothing".
</details>

---

## 8. How deep is the determinant? Depth and rigidity

Knowing $\det M \neq 0$, one may ask *how close to zero* it is. The natural yardstick is the $\pi$-adic order.

{{algorithm:1}}

{{visualization:1}}

The left panel is striking: in every case sampled, the $\pi$-adic depth is *exactly* $\binom n 2$. Only the inequality $\geq$ is proved; equality is the sharpest open question in the subject, and it reduces to a single Vandermonde-versus-superfactorial identity.

The right panel shows the consequence that the depth bound has for the counter itself:

> **Rigidity theorem.** If $\binom n 2 \geq p-1$, then all the values $c_{S,T}(r)$ are **congruent modulo $p$**.

<details>
<summary><b>Why rigidity follows from depth</b></summary>

Write the determinant as the image of the integer polynomial $F(X) = \sum_r c_{S,T}(r)X^{r}$ in $\mathbb{Z}[X]/(\Phi_p)$. Divisibility by $\pi^{p-1}$ in that quotient becomes divisibility of the mod-$p$ reduction by $(X-1)^{p-1}$. Over $\mathbb{F}_p$ one has the identity
$$(X-1)^{p-1} = 1 + X + \dots + X^{p-1}$$
(multiply both sides by $X-1$ and use the Frobenius identity). A polynomial of degree less than $p$ divisible by that geometric sum must be a *constant multiple* of it — so all its coefficients coincide.
</details>

The dichotomy that results is stark: in the rigid regime, **either** the counter is nonzero at every one of the $p$ residues, **or** it reaches absolute value at least $p$ somewhere. There is no middle ground.

---

## 9. The composite side: how wide can a closed gap be?

Over composite moduli the gap does close, and one can ask for the largest width at which it can. The naive construction — $S_i = ai$, $T_j = bj$ over $m = ab$, making all exponents zero — only reaches $n \le \sqrt m$. A much better mechanism is a **sign-reversing involution**:

> **Pigeonhole criterion.** Suppose there is a set $J$ of rows and a subgroup $B \le \mathbb{Z}/m$ such that the $S$-values in $J$ annihilate $B$, and the columns fall into fewer than $|J|$ classes modulo $B$. Then for *every* permutation, two columns of the same class are matched to rows of $J$; swapping them preserves the exponent and flips the sign, so everything cancels.

{{algorithm:3}}

This reaches every width $2 \le n \le m - q$ with $q$ the least prime factor. Combined with the fact that the top two widths are always open, the answer is **exact for even moduli**:

> Over an even modulus $m \geq 4$, the parity gap closes at width $n \geq 2$ **if and only if** $n \le m-2$.

---

## 10. Why anyone outside algebra should care: uncertainty

Chebotarev's theorem is exactly equivalent to the sharpest uncertainty principle available on a finite cyclic group.

> **Additive uncertainty principle.** For prime $p$ and every nonzero $f \colon \mathbb{Z}/p \to \mathbb{C}$,
> $$|\operatorname{supp} f| + |\operatorname{supp}\hat f| \;\ge\; p+1 .$$

The classical [Donoho–Stark bound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncertainty_principle) $|\operatorname{supp} f|\cdot|\operatorname{supp}\hat f| \ge p$ holds over any cyclic group; the *additive* strengthening is a purely prime phenomenon, and it implies the multiplicative one since $ab+1 \ge a+b$.

Explore it directly — build a signal by clicking, and watch its spectrum:

{{interactive_demo:1}}

<details>
<summary><b>Why it is the same theorem</b></summary>

Suppose $f$ lives on a set $A$ and $\hat f$ dies on a set $C$ with $|A| = |C| = n$. Restricting the Fourier matrix to rows $C$ and columns $A$, the pair of conditions says exactly that this $n \times n$ submatrix has a nonzero kernel vector — that it is *singular*. Chebotarev's theorem forbids singular minors over a prime modulus, so no such $f$ exists, and $|A| + |\operatorname{supp}\hat f| \ge p+1$.

Over a composite modulus $m = ab$, singular minors are everywhere, and the standard witness is the indicator of the subgroup of order $a$: it has support $a$ and spectrum of support $b$, so the sum $a+b$ can be as small as $2\sqrt m$.
</details>

The practical payoff is exact sparse recovery:

> A $k$-sparse signal on $\mathbb{Z}/p$ is uniquely determined by **any** $2k$ of its Fourier coefficients, provided $2k \le p$.

If two $k$-sparse signals agreed on $2k$ frequencies, their difference would be $2k$-sparse with $2k$ vanishing Fourier coefficients — a support sum of at most $p$, which the theorem forbids. Over composite moduli this fails, and the counterexamples are precisely the subgroup indicators above.

{{demo:1}}

---

Finally, a single script that walks through every result on this page and checks it computationally: the mass identity, the determinant identity, exhaustive verification of nonvanishing for small primes, minimal-length witnesses, closure over composites, the exact width for even moduli, the uncertainty principle, $\pi$-adic depth, and the rigidity dichotomy.

{{demo:0}}

---

## 12. Where the frontier is

Two questions stand out.

**Exact depth.** Is $v_\pi(\det M) = \binom n2$ for every $n \le p$? The lower bound is proved and finiteness is Chebotarev's theorem; the missing piece is a single coefficient. In the multilinear Taylor expansion the unique minimal term is the one with orders $\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$, with coefficient the bialternant

$$\frac{\prod_{i<j}(S_j - S_i)(T_j - T_i)}{\prod_{k<n} k!},$$

whose denominator is invertible modulo $p$ exactly when $n \le p$. The whole obstruction is a finite identity about determinants of binomial-coefficient matrices.

**Exact rigidity.** Is the counter constant modulo $p^m$ whenever $\binom n2 \ge m(p-1)$, with $\lfloor \binom n2/(p-1)\rfloor$ the largest such $m$? The case $m=1$ is settled.

And on the composite side: is the pigeonhole construction optimal, i.e. is the maximal closure width exactly $m-q$ for every composite $m$? The even case is settled; the first open case is $m=9$, where the answer is either $6$ or $7$.

---

### A closing thought

The parity-gap question began as pure combinatorics: can even and odd matchings cancel at every residue? The answer for primes is no, and the reason has nothing to do with counting. It is that $p$ ramifies completely in the cyclotomic field, that reduction at the ramified prime fuses $n$ distinct roots of unity into one root of multiplicity $n$, and that a polynomial with few terms cannot afford a root of high multiplicity in characteristic $p$. That chain — from permutation signs, through ramification, to sparse polynomials — is also what underwrites the sharpest known uncertainty principle on a cyclic group, and with it the exact-recovery guarantees of sparse Fourier sampling.

theorem X_sub_one_pow_eq_geom_sum :
    ((X : (ZMod p)[X]) - 1) ^ (p - 1) = ∑ i ∈ range p, X ^ i := by

    intro h
    have := congrArg (fun q => Polynomial.coeff q 1) h

    (cyclotomic p ℤ).map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) = ((X : (ZMod p)[X]) - 1) ^ (p - 1) := by

  have hterm : ∀ r : ZMod p, (C (permCoeffZ S T r) * X ^ (r.val) : ℤ[X]).coeff k
      = if r = (k : ZMod p) then permCoeffZ S T r else 0 := by
    intro r
    rw [Polynomial.coeff_C_mul, Polynomial.coeff_X_pow]
    by_cases hr : r = (k : ZMod p)
    · subst hr
      simp [ZMod.val_natCast_of_lt hk]
    · have : r.val ≠ k := by
        intro hval
        apply hr
        rw [← hval, ZMod.natCast_val, ZMod.cast_id]
      simp [Ne.symm this, hr]
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun r _ => hterm r), Finset.sum_ite_eq' univ ((k : ZMod p))]
  simp

/-- The minor is the class of the generating polynomial evaluated at `ζ`. -/
theorem det_zpow_eq_mk_counterPoly (S T : Fin n → ZMod p) :
    (Matrix.of fun j k : Fin n => zpow p (S j * T k)).det
      = AdjoinRoot.mk (cyclotomic p ℤ) (counterPoly S T) := by
  classical
  have hsplit : ∑ r : ZMod p, (permCoeffZ S T r) • zpow p r
      = ∑ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), (Equiv.Perm.sign σ : ℤ) • zpow p (permExp S T σ) := by
    have hterm : ∀ r : ZMod p, (permCoeffZ S T r) • zpow p r
        = ∑ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
            if permExp S T σ = r then (Equiv.Perm.sign σ : ℤ) • zpow p r else 0 := by
      intro r
      rw [permCoeffZ, Finset.sum_filter, Finset.sum_smul]
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun σ _ => ?_
      split_ifs <;> simp
    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun r _ => hterm r, Finset.sum_comm]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun σ _ => ?_
    rw [Finset.sum_eq_single (permExp S T σ)]
    · simp
    · intro r _ hr; simp [Ne.symm hr]
    · intro h; exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ (permExp S T σ)) h
  rw [det_zetaPow_eq_sum_permCoeff, ← hsplit, counterPoly, map_sum]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun r _ => ?_
  rw [map_mul, map_pow, AdjoinRoot.mk_X, AdjoinRoot.mk_C, zpow, zsmul_eq_mul, ← zeta]
  simp

/-! ## Rigidity -/

/-- **Mod-`p` rigidity of the parity counter.**  If the `π`-adic depth `n(n-1)/2` of the minor
reaches the ramification index `p - 1`, the parity-weighted exponent counter is constant modulo
`p`: all of its values are congruent to each other. -/
theorem permCoeffZ_congr_of_pi_depth (hpn : p - 1 ≤ ∑ i ∈ range n, i) (S T : Fin n → ZMod p)
    (r r' : ZMod p) : (p : ℤ) ∣ permCoeffZ S T r - permCoeffZ S T r' := by
  have hdvd : pi p ^ (p - 1) ∣ AdjoinRoot.mk (cyclotomic p ℤ) (counterPoly S T) := by
    rw [← det_zpow_eq_mk_counterPoly]
    exact dvd_trans (pow_dvd_pow _ hpn) (pi_pow_dvd_det_zpow S T)
  have hred := X_sub_one_pow_dvd_of_pi_pow_dvd (le_refl (p - 1)) _ hdvd
  set g : (ZMod p)[X] := (counterPoly S T).map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) with hg
  have hdeg : g.natDegree < p :=
    lt_of_le_of_lt (Polynomial.natDegree_map_le) (counterPoly_natDegree_lt S T)
  have hcoeff := coeff_eq_coeff_of_X_sub_one_pow_dvd g hdeg hred (ZMod.val_lt r) (ZMod.val_lt r')
  have hmapcoeff : ∀ s : ZMod p, g.coeff s.val = ((permCoeffZ S T s : ℤ) : ZMod p) := by
    intro s
    rw [hg, Polynomial.coeff_map, coeff_counterPoly S T (ZMod.val_lt s)]
    simp [ZMod.natCast_val, ZMod.cast_id]
  rw [hmapcoeff r, hmapcoeff r'] at hcoeff
  have : ((permCoeffZ S T r - permCoeffZ S T r' : ℤ) : ZMod p) = 0 := by
    push_cast
    rw [hcoeff]
    ring
  exact (ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd _ p).mp this

/-- **Dichotomy in the rigid regime.**  If `p - 1 ≤ n(n-1)/2` and `S`, `T` are injective, then
either the counter is nonzero at *every* residue, or the parity gap is at least `p`: some residue
carries a parity excess of absolute value `≥ p`.  (Both alternatives are far stronger than the
bare nonvanishing supplied by Conjecture A.) -/
theorem full_support_or_large_gap (hpn : p - 1 ≤ ∑ i ∈ range n, i) (S T : Fin n → ZMod p)
    (hS : Function.Injective S) (hT : Function.Injective T) :
    (∀ r : ZMod p, permCoeffZ S T r ≠ 0) ∨ ∃ r : ZMod p, (p : ℤ) ≤ |permCoeffZ S T r| := by
  by_cases hall : ∀ r : ZMod p, permCoeffZ S T r ≠ 0
  · exact Or.inl hall
  · right
    push_neg at hall
    obtain ⟨r₀, hr₀⟩ := hall
    obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := exists_permCoeff_ne_zero S T hS hT
    have hrZ : permCoeffZ S T r ≠ 0 := by
      intro h
      apply hr
      rw [← permCoeffZ_cast, h]
      simp
    have hdvd : (p : ℤ) ∣ permCoeffZ S T r := by
      have := permCoeffZ_congr_of_pi_depth hpn S T r r₀
      rwa [hr₀, sub_zero] at this
    exact ⟨r, Int.le_of_dvd (abs_pos.mpr hrZ) ((dvd_abs _ _).mpr hdvd)⟩

/-! ## Support versus height -/

/-- **Support-or-height dichotomy.**  Either every value of the parity-weighted counter is
divisible by `p`, or the counter is supported on more than `min (n(n-1)/2) (p-1)` residues.  The
`π`-adic depth of the minor is thus converted into a *lower bound on the support* through the
characteristic-`p` sparsity lemma. -/
theorem large_support_or_p_dvd (S T : Fin n → ZMod p) :
    (∀ r : ZMod p, (p : ℤ) ∣ permCoeffZ S T r) ∨
      min (∑ i ∈ range n, i) (p - 1) + 1 ≤
        (univ.filter (fun r : ZMod p => permCoeffZ S T r ≠ 0)).card := by
  classical
  set g : (ZMod p)[X] := (counterPoly S T).map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) with hg
  have hcoeff : ∀ r : ZMod p, g.coeff r.val = ((permCoeffZ S T r : ℤ) : ZMod p) := by
    intro r
    rw [hg, Polynomial.coeff_map, coeff_counterPoly S T (ZMod.val_lt r)]
    simp [ZMod.natCast_val, ZMod.cast_id]
  by_cases hg0 : g = 0
  · left
    intro r
    have h0 : ((permCoeffZ S T r : ℤ) : ZMod p) = 0 := by rw [← hcoeff r, hg0]; simp
    exact (ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd _ p).mp h0
  · right
    set m : ℕ := min (∑ i ∈ range n, i) (p - 1) with hm
    have hdvdpi : pi p ^ m ∣ AdjoinRoot.mk (cyclotomic p ℤ) (counterPoly S T) := by
      rw [← det_zpow_eq_mk_counterPoly]
      exact dvd_trans (pow_dvd_pow _ (min_le_left _ _)) (pi_pow_dvd_det_zpow S T)
    have hdvd : ((X : (ZMod p)[X]) - 1) ^ m ∣ g :=
      X_sub_one_pow_dvd_of_pi_pow_dvd (min_le_right _ _) _ hdvdpi
    have hdeg : g.natDegree < p :=
      lt_of_le_of_lt Polynomial.natDegree_map_le (counterPoly_natDegree_lt S T)
    have hcard := lt_card_support_of_X_sub_one_pow_dvd m g hg0 hdeg hdvd
    have hsub : g.support.card ≤ (univ.filter (fun r : ZMod p => permCoeffZ S T r ≠ 0)).card := by
      refine Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (fun k => (k : ZMod p)) ?_ ?_
      · intro k hk
        have hklt : k < p := lt_of_le_of_lt (Polynomial.le_natDegree_of_mem_supp k hk) hdeg
        have hne : g.coeff k ≠ 0 := Polynomial.mem_support_iff.mp hk
        refine Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
        intro hzero
        apply hne
        have hval : ((k : ZMod p)).val = k := ZMod.val_natCast_of_lt hklt
        rw [← hval, hcoeff ((k : ZMod p)), hzero]

      · intro a ha b hb hab
        have halt : a < p := lt_of_le_of_lt (Polynomial.le_natDegree_of_mem_supp a ha) hdeg
        have hblt : b < p := lt_of_le_of_lt (Polynomial.le_natDegree_of_mem_supp b hb) hdeg
        have hv := congrArg ZMod.val hab

    omega

/-- **Support-or-height for injective data.**  Combining the previous dichotomy with

theorem large_support_or_large_gap (S T : Fin n → ZMod p) (hS : Function.Injective S)

  · right

    have hrZ : permCoeffZ S T r ≠ 0 := by

      apply hr
      rw [← permCoeffZ_cast, h]
      simp
    exact ⟨r, Int.le_of_dvd (abs_pos.mpr hrZ) ((dvd_abs _ _).mpr (hall r))⟩
  · exact Or.inl hcard

reducing the determinant modulo `p`: as soon as `n(n-1)/2 ≥ p - 1`, the whole minor is divisible

theorem sum_range_card_le_sum (s : Finset ℕ) : ∑ i ∈ range s.card, i ≤ ∑ x ∈ s, x := by
  classical
  set e : ℕ ↪ ℤ := ⟨fun x => (x : ℤ), fun x y h => by simpa using h⟩ with he

    intro x hx
    rw [ht, Finset.mem_map] at hx

    rw [ht, Finset.sum_map]
    simp [he]

      = (∏ i, (u i) ^ ((K i : ℕ))) • (Matrix.detRowAlternating : (Fin n → R) [⋀^Fin n]→ₗ[R] R)

    have h2 : (∏ i, t ^ ((K i : ℕ))) ∣ ∏ i, (u i) ^ ((K i : ℕ)) :=
      Finset.prod_dvd_prod_of_dvd _ _ (fun i _ => pow_dvd_pow_of_dvd (hu i) _)
    have h3 : (∏ i : Fin n, t ^ ((K i : ℕ))) = t ^ (∑ i, (K i : ℕ)) :=

      rw [Function.not_injective_iff] at hinj

      AlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_eq _ _ (by rw [hij]) hne
    rw [hzero, mul_zero]
    exact dvd_zero _

/-- **The `π`-adic depth of an integral DFT minor.** -/
theorem pi_pow_dvd_det_zetaPow (a b : Fin n → ℕ) (hb : ∀ j, b j < p) :
    pi p ^ (∑ i ∈ range n, i) ∣ (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin n => zeta p ^ (a i * b j)).det := by
  classical
  set u : Fin n → CycRing p := fun i => zeta p ^ (a i) - 1 with hu
  have hudvd : ∀ i, pi p ∣ u i := by
    intro i
    have h := sub_dvd_pow_sub_pow (zeta p) 1 (a i)
    simpa [pi, hu] using h
  set w : Fin p → (Fin n → CycRing p) := fun k j => (((b j).choose (k : ℕ) : ℕ) : CycRing p)
    with hw
  have hrow : (fun i j : Fin n => zeta p ^ (a i * b j))
      = fun i => ∑ k : Fin p, (u i) ^ (k : ℕ) • w k := by
    funext i j
    have hexp : (u i + 1) ^ (b j) = ∑ k ∈ range (b j + 1),
        (u i) ^ k * (((b j).choose k : ℕ) : CycRing p) := by
      rw [add_pow]
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun k _ => ?_
      rw [one_pow, mul_one]
    have hu1 : u i + 1 = zeta p ^ (a i) := by rw [hu]; ring
    have hext : ∑ k ∈ range (b j + 1), (u i) ^ k * (((b j).choose k : ℕ) : CycRing p)
        = ∑ k ∈ range p, (u i) ^ k * (((b j).choose k : ℕ) : CycRing p) := by
      have hsub : range (b j + 1) ⊆ range p := by
        intro x hx
        simp only [Finset.mem_range] at hx ⊢
        have := hb j
        omega
      refine Finset.sum_subset hsub ?_
      intro k hkp hk
      simp only [Finset.mem_range, not_lt] at hkp hk
      have hz : (b j).choose k = 0 := Nat.choose_eq_zero_of_lt (by omega)
      rw [hz]
      simp
    have hfin : ∑ k ∈ range p, (u i) ^ k * (((b j).choose k : ℕ) : CycRing p)
        = ∑ k : Fin p, (u i) ^ (k : ℕ) • w k j := by
      have hterm : ∀ k : Fin p, (u i) ^ (k : ℕ) • w k j
          = (u i) ^ (k : ℕ) * (((b j).choose (k : ℕ) : ℕ) : CycRing p) := by
        intro k
        simp [hw, smul_eq_mul]
      symm
      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun k _ => hterm k),
        Fin.sum_univ_eq_sum_range (fun k => (u i) ^ k * (((b j).choose k : ℕ) : CycRing p)) p]
    calc zeta p ^ (a i * b j) = (zeta p ^ (a i)) ^ (b j) := by rw [pow_mul]
      _ = (u i + 1) ^ (b j) := by rw [hu1]
      _ = ∑ k ∈ range (b j + 1), (u i) ^ k * (((b j).choose k : ℕ) : CycRing p) := hexp
      _ = ∑ k ∈ range p, (u i) ^ k * (((b j).choose k : ℕ) : CycRing p) := hext
      _ = ∑ k : Fin p, (u i) ^ (k : ℕ) • w k j := hfin
      _ = (∑ k : Fin p, (u i) ^ (k : ℕ) • w k) j := by simp
  have hdet : (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin n => zeta p ^ (a i * b j)).det
      = Matrix.detRowAlternating (fun i => ∑ k : Fin p, (u i) ^ (k : ℕ) • w k) := by
    rw [← hrow]
    rfl
  rw [hdet]
  exact pow_dvd_det_of_rows_taylor (pi p) u hudvd w

/-- The same bound for the minor written in terms of the character `zpow`. -/
theorem pi_pow_dvd_det_zpow (S T : Fin n → ZMod p) :
    pi p ^ (∑ i ∈ range n, i) ∣ (Matrix.of fun j k : Fin n => zpow p (S j * T k)).det := by
  have hcong : (Matrix.of fun j k : Fin n => zpow p (S j * T k))
      = Matrix.of fun j k : Fin n => zeta p ^ ((S j).val * (T k).val) := by
    funext j k
    exact zpow_mul_eq (S j) (T k)
  rw [hcong]
  exact pi_pow_dvd_det_zetaPow (fun j => (S j).val) (fun k => (T k).val)
    (fun k => ZMod.val_lt (T k))


/-! ## Exactness of the depth bound in the base case `n = 2` -/

/-- Divisibility by `π` is detected by the reduction `red : ℤ[ζ_p] → 𝔽_p`. -/
theorem red_eq_zero_of_pi_dvd {y : CycRing p} (h : pi p ∣ y) : red p y = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨z, rfl⟩ := h
  rw [map_mul, red_pi, zero_mul]

/-- `ζ^d - 1` has `π`-adic order exactly one for `0 < d < p`. -/
theorem pi_sq_not_dvd_zeta_pow_sub_one {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) (hdp : d < p) :
    ¬ (pi p ^ 2 ∣ zeta p ^ d - 1) := by
  have hfac : zeta p ^ d - 1 = pi p * ∑ i ∈ range d, zeta p ^ i := by
    rw [pi, mul_comm]
    exact (geom_sum_mul (zeta p) d).symm
  intro hdvd
  rw [hfac, sq] at hdvd
  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hdvd
  have hcancel : ∑ i ∈ range d, zeta p ^ i = pi p * z :=
    mul_left_cancel₀ (pi_ne_zero p) (by rw [hz]; ring)
  have hred : red p (∑ i ∈ range d, zeta p ^ i) = (d : ZMod p) := by
    simp [map_sum]
  rw [hcancel, red_eq_zero_of_pi_dvd ⟨z, rfl⟩] at hred
  have hne : ((d : ZMod p)) ≠ 0 := by
    rw [Ne, ZMod.natCast_eq_zero_iff]
    intro hdvd'
    have := Nat.le_of_dvd hd hdvd'
    omega
  exact hne hred.symm

/-- **The depth bound is exact for `n = 2`.**  For injective `S, T : Fin 2 → ZMod p` the
`2 × 2` minor has `π`-adic order exactly `1 = 2·1/2`, confirming the expected value
`n(n-1)/2` in the base case. -/
theorem pi_sq_not_dvd_det_two (S T : Fin 2 → ZMod p) (hS : Function.Injective S)
    (hT : Function.Injective T) :
    ¬ (pi p ^ 2 ∣ (Matrix.of fun j k : Fin 2 => zpow p (S j * T k)).det) := by
  set B : ZMod p := S 0 * T 1 + S 1 * T 0 with hB
  set D : ZMod p := (S 0 - S 1) * (T 0 - T 1) with hD
  have hDne : D ≠ 0 := by
    have h0 : S 0 - S 1 ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr (fun h => by simpa using hS h)
    have h1 : T 0 - T 1 ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr (fun h => by simpa using hT h)
    exact mul_ne_zero h0 h1
  have hdet : (Matrix.of fun j k : Fin 2 => zpow p (S j * T k)).det
      = zpow p B * (zpow p D - 1) := by
    rw [Matrix.det_fin_two]
    have hsum : S 0 * T 0 + S 1 * T 1 = B + D := by rw [hB, hD]; ring

The refinement asked for in Conjecture A speaks of a permutation of *minimal Coxeter length*.
This file supplies the notion and its basic theory in the shape needed there:

* `ParityGap.coxeterLength σ` — the number of inversions of `σ`, i.e. the length of `σ` in the
  Coxeter presentation of the symmetric group by adjacent transpositions;
* `ParityGap.sign_eq_neg_one_pow_coxeterLength` — the sign character is the parity of the

open Equiv Equiv.Perm Finset

order is reversed by `σ`. -/
def inversions (σ : Perm (Fin n)) : Finset (Σ _ : Fin n, Fin n) :=
  (Equiv.Perm.finPairsLT n).filter (fun x => σ x.1 < σ x.2)

/-- The **Coxeter length** of a permutation: its number of inversions. -/
def coxeterLength (σ : Perm (Fin n)) : ℕ := (inversions σ).card

theorem sign_eq_signAux (σ : Perm (Fin n)) : Equiv.Perm.sign σ = Equiv.Perm.signAux σ := by
  induction σ using Equiv.Perm.swap_induction_on with
  | one => simp
  | @swap_mul f x y hxy ih =>
    rw [map_mul, Equiv.Perm.sign_swap hxy, Equiv.Perm.signAux_mul, Equiv.Perm.signAux_swap hxy, ih]

/-- **The sign is the parity of the Coxeter length.** -/

    Equiv.Perm.sign σ = (-1 : ℤˣ) ^ (coxeterLength σ) := by
  classical
  have hfilter : (Equiv.Perm.finPairsLT n).filter (fun x => σ x.1 ≤ σ x.2) = inversions σ := by
    refine Finset.filter_congr fun x hx => ?_
    have hlt : x.2 < x.1 := Equiv.Perm.mem_finPairsLT.mp hx
    have hne : σ x.1 ≠ σ x.2 := fun h => absurd (σ.injective h) (ne_of_gt hlt)
    exact ⟨fun h => lt_of_le_of_ne h hne, le_of_lt⟩
  rw [sign_eq_signAux, Equiv.Perm.signAux, coxeterLength, ← hfilter, Finset.prod_ite]
  simp

  classical
  rw [coxeterLength, inversions, Finset.card_eq_zero, Finset.filter_eq_empty_iff]
  intro x hx
  have hlt : x.2 < x.1 := Equiv.Perm.mem_finPairsLT.mp hx
  simpa using hlt.le

/-- Only the identity permutation has no inversions. -/

  classical
  constructor
  · intro h
    have hno : ∀ x ∈ Equiv.Perm.finPairsLT n, ¬ (σ x.1 < σ x.2) := by
      intro x hx hlt
      have : x ∈ inversions σ := Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hx, hlt⟩
      rw [coxeterLength, Finset.card_eq_zero] at h
      simp [h] at this
    have hmono : StrictMono σ := by
      intro a b hab
      have hmem : (⟨b, a⟩ : Σ _ : Fin n, Fin n) ∈ Equiv.Perm.finPairsLT n :=
        Equiv.Perm.mem_finPairsLT.mpr hab
      have := hno _ hmem
      have hne : σ b ≠ σ a := fun hc => absurd (σ.injective hc) (ne_of_gt hab)

    -- a strictly monotone permutation of a finite linear order is the identity
    ext a
    have hiso : ∀ a : Fin n, a ≤ σ a := fun a => hmono.le_apply
    have hiso' : ∀ a : Fin n, a ≤ σ.symm a := by
      intro a
      have hmono' : StrictMono σ.symm := by
        intro x y hxy
        by_contra hc
        push_neg at hc

          exact absurd this (not_lt.mpr hxy.le)

    have h3 : σ a ≤ a := by
      have := hiso' (σ a)
      simpa using this
    exact le_antisymm h3 h1
  · rintro rfl
    exact coxeterLength_one

end ParityGap",
